A: Sagittal T2-weighted MRI of the lumbosacral spine from an adult patient with tethered cord syndrome (article title: cesarean section under epidural anesthesia in tethered cord syndrome; in-text notes prior sacrocolpopexy and planned cesarean section). The red arrow marks a low-lying conus medullaris at the L5 level, the classic MRI hallmark of tethered cord syndrome, matching the vocabulary finding tethered_cord_syndrome_low_lying_conus. B: Three-dimensional volume-rendered CT reconstruction of the sacrum in the same patient with tethered cord syndrome; the red arrow indicates spina bifida in the sacral region. Sacral spina bifida (spina bifida occulta) is a classic associated spinal-dysraphism lesion of this tethered cord case, directly captioned as part of the same figure. The specific finding is not in the allowed vocabulary, so it is recorded as a proposed finding rather than a vocabulary finding_key.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Transverse lumbar MRI of a real patient showing fibrotic strands in the posterior aspect of the spinal cord (red arrow), a recognized MRI feature of tethered cord syndrome corresponding to a thickened/tight filum terminale. Disease attribution is supported by the article title ('Complicated Neuraxial Anesthesia in a Patient With Tethered Spinal Cord') and the in-text mention of tethering. B: Sagittal lumbar MRI of a real patient showing a tethered spinal cord (white arrow) with an unusually low-lying conus medullaris (yellow arrow) at the L3 level, confirmed by the in-text mention of 'atypically low conus medullaris at the L3 level suggesting tethering.' This is a diagnostic MRI manifestation of tethered cord syndrome, explicitly labeled as unusual/atypical in both caption and text.
